elements_not_encoded.reason: "Yes" arrow from Q2 into the some-dehydration box; the branch is the any2 in Diagnose probable some dehydration in cholera.

elements_not_encoded.text: Give oral rehydration solution (ORS) 75mL/kg (or at least 2-4L) over 4 hours.
Give additional ORS (as much as tolerated) after each episode of diarrhoea/ vomiting.
Insert 2 large bore IV lines, if possible.
Give Ringer's lactate IV fluid as first fluid choice. If unavailable, give sodium chloride 0.9% IV:
Give 30mL/kg IV over first 30 minutes, then give 70mL/kg over next 2.5 hours, while awaiting transfer.
If transport delayed > 3 hours: continue 5mL/kg/hour IV.
If unable to insert IV line and patient able to drink, give oral rehydration solution (ORS) 30mL/kg over first 30 minutes, then 70mL/ kg over next 2.5 hours.
elements_not_encoded.reason: ORS if no IV line; management.

elements_not_encoded.reason: NGT ORS if no IV line and decreased consciousness; management.

elements_not_encoded.text: If no better or worse, discuss with referral centre.

elements_not_encoded.text: If awake, able to drink and pulse < 100, continue IV fluids, but also manage as some dehydration: give ORS 75mL/kg (or at least 2-4L) over 4 hours.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Reassessment after IV fluids (awake, able to drink, pulse < 100 -> also ORS) is a response to treatment; the language cannot tell a reassessment from the first assessment, and the action is management.

elements_not_encoded.text: Manage as severe dehydration and refer urgently (see adjacent).
elements_not_encoded.reason: Red box 4 follows the hourly reassessment after ORS (signs of dehydration or ongoing diarrhoea/vomiting). The language cannot tell a post-treatment reassessment from the first assessment; encoding it would make ongoing diarrhoea alone Urgent at presentation, contradicting Q1/Q2.

judgment_calls.topic: Q1 = No in the some-dehydration rule
judgment_calls.decision: Written as recorded "No" answers (no X) for each any-of sign, and any2 of "No" over the three >=2-of groups (i.e. at most one positive). (not …) was tried first, but VHA's evidence walker throws "Not supported not", so it cannot be used.
judgment_calls.alternatives: Omit Q1 = No entirely (some dehydration would also be diagnosed in severe cases; both are Urgent anyway).

judgment_calls.decision: Exposure to (contextual qualifier) + Vibrio cholerae (organism), with onset within 5 days.
judgment_calls.alternatives: History of travel with high risk of exposure to communicable disease (situation); Exposure to Vibrio cholerae is an event, not usable in a finding.

judgment_calls.decision: No probable Severe dehydration diagnosis: the page says "manage as severe dehydration", not "likely". The red box becomes Urgent directly from the Q1 findings, anchored on active cholera.
judgment_calls.alternatives: A probable Severe dehydration rule referenced from the priority evaluation.

judgment_calls.decision: Urgent for both red boxes ("refer urgently"). Several Q1 signs are warning signs that carry their own (higher) priority.
judgment_calls.alternatives: Very urgent/Emergency for severe dehydration; the page does not escalate explicitly.
Urgent on cholera + ongoing diarrhoea/vomiting or any dehydration sign, which would fire at first presentation.
